- Provide a representative prompt set and expected evaluation metrics so our legal and product teams can assess risk.

Jake — really appreciate the clear asks and the samples. Moving forward with the plan below unless you want to tweak.

Proposed scope (high-level):
1) Ingest your sample bundle and run a long-context evaluation suite covering: truncation thresholds, progressive-context summarization fidelity (50k, 80k, 120k slices where feasible), and downstream QA prompts you highlighted.
2) Models we recommend testing (initial pass):
   - rw-llama3-70b-q4f (recommended: quantized Llama-3 family; good balance of fidelity + throughput)
   - mistral-instruct-8x (strong instruction-following for summarization)
   - redwood-long-128k-experimental (if you'd like to test extended-window capability; availability varies by region)
3) Deliverables: evaluation report (CSV results + qualitative samples), recommended prompt set (we'll normalize your prompts), summary of truncation behaviors and suggested mitigations (prefix caching, chunked summarization patterns), and a short walkthrough session.

Timeline & cost (estimate):
- Dry run (sanity checks on a 5 doc subset): 3 business days
- Full eval: 7–10 business days after dry run signoff
- Cost: estimate ~$2.5k–$4k depending on chosen models & extended-window runtime for redwood-long-128k. We can tighten after we run the dry run.

Security/compliance notes: we are happy to run evals in Private mode if you prefer the bundle never leave your VPC. For SOC2 evidence, attaching our standard SOC2 overview and the security one-pager link.

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm: (a) which models you'd like in the initial pass, (b) whether you need Private mode, and (c) signoff for the dry run.
- If approved, I'll create a mutual action plan + HubSpot deal entry (I'll include the DocuSign link if you need an SCA).

On availability — I can kick off the dry run tomorrow afternoon if you approve.

Best,

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Long-context evals — follow-up & next steps

Adding a quick technical note on context handling and evaluation methodology so expectations are aligned.

- Truncation behavior: For models with native 32k windows (most non-extended variants), we will test (a) naive truncation (drop earliest tokens), (b) prefix-preserving sliding window, and (c) chunk-and-merge summarization (summarize chunks then summarize summaries). We'll include token-level debug outputs so you can see which clauses get dropped.
- Long-window runs: redwood-long-128k-experimental will allow us to test single-pass summarization across 80k docs; however, extended-window runs are ~2–3x the compute and may increase cost/time.
- Fidelity measurement: we'll use ROUGE/L and a custom clause-presence checklist (binary flags for critical clauses you supplied). We'll also sample human-reviewed summaries for a small subset (5–10 documents) to calibrate the automatic metrics.
- Caching & latency: if you plan to serve in production, prefix KV caching should preserve repeated static preambles (e.g., TOC pages) and reduce repeated compute. We'll include the predicted token-cost per request for each model setup.

I can prepare a reproducible eval script (notebook + runbook) as part of deliverables.

-Ethan
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ethan_park@redwood.ai

Example failing-case mitigation (preview):

- Mitigation: 1) pre-annotate critical clause anchors (regexes) and instruct prompt to prioritize clause-preserving compression; 2) chunk-and-merge summarization with clause-aware heuristics; or 3) fall back to a structured extraction pipeline for clauses before summarization. We'll include concrete examples from your sample set in the report.
